content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels of itraconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both drugs are administered in their oral forms. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing the metabolism of itraconazole through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is also unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction remains unclear. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. For patients starting abemaciclib at doses of 150 mg or 200 mg twice daily, the dose should be reduced to 100 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If the dose of abemaciclib has already been reduced to 100 mg twice daily due to adverse reactions, further reduce the dose to 50 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased (after 3–5 half-lives of the inhibitor) to the dose used prior to starting the inhibitor. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Coadministration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Coadministration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and the risk of its toxicities. Itraconazole increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Consider using an alternative medication with no or minimal potential to inhibit CYP3A4. If concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, consider delaying ado-trastuzumab until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitors have cleared from the circulation (~3 elimination half-lives of the inhibitors). If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is coadministered and ado-trastuzumab cannot be delayed, closely monitor for adverse reactions. Itraconazole increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If afatinib is not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of afatinib by 10 mg. Albuterol and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels of alfuzosin by decreasing its metabolism. Both alfuzosin and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider using an alternative drug with no or minimal potential to inhibit CYP3A4. If concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and consider decreasing the alfentanil dose as necessary. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid concomitant use of almotriptan and potent CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after itraconazole. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of alvimopan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both amiodarone and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. Coadministration of amiodarone and a QT-prolonging agent may result in additive effects on the QT interval and increase the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Amisulpride and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministered. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both itraconazole and amitriptyline increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting its metabolism and through other mechanisms. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) elicit negative inotropic effects, which may be additive to those of itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions, and dose reduction of the concomitant drug may be necessary. Itraconazole and anagrelide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concurrent use 2 weeks before and during itraconazole treatment. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if medication must be coadministered. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. For patients receiving apixaban 5 or 10 mg twice daily, decrease the apixaban dose by 50% when coadministered with drugs that are both P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. For patients receiving apixaban 5 mg twice daily, avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Apomorphine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Arformoterol and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Consider reducing the aripiprazole dose when combining a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor with a less potent CYP2D6 inhibitor. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Arsenic trioxide and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Artemether and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both itraconazole and artemether/lumefantrine increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole and asenapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Asenapine transdermal and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels of ateviridine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Atomoxetine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Limit atorvastatin dose to 20 mg/day. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during and 2 weeks after itraconazole. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If unable to avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. Azithromycin and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration of bedaquiline with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit of treatment outweighs the risk. Both bedaquiline and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inducing its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If unable to avoid coadministration of belzutifan with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose in accordance with its prescribing information. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone (benzhydrocodone is a prodrug of hydrocodone) plasma concentrations and can result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. Itraconazole increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely.
